To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

AI is an emergent, complex system of human and artificial intelligence, that AI is not a thing or a technology, that AI is the process of creating and applying AI technologies and systems, that AI technologies are not the same thing as AI, that the law of the elephant is a metaphor for understanding and applying AI technologies, and that AI technologies are the elephant in the room of legal education, legal scholarship, and legal practice.

(1) lawyers' understanding of AI and the law are insufficient, (2) lawyers are not sufficiently competent in AI, (3) lawyers' understanding and competence in AI is essential to the legal profession and to the public interest, (4) lawyers' understanding is essential to the public interest and to their professional responsibility, (5) lawyers are not equipped to address the AI crisis, and (6) law schools must address the AI crisis.

(a) the law and legal profession have not yet adequately understood the AI technologies and their potential harms; and (b) the law and the legal profession must understand the technologies and harms before they can adequately respond to them.
